html:
Leo Africanus was born in Granada, grew up in Fez, and visited Timbuktu about 1510 with his uncle, an envoy. The city then belonged to the Songhai Empire of Askia Muhammad. Later, as a captive in Rome, he wrote a description of Africa. This is John Pory's English translation of 1600, in its old spelling. Tombuto is Timbuktu and Barbarie is North Africa.

When I my selfe was here, I saw one camels loade of salt sold for 80. ducates. The rich king of Tombuto hath many plates and scepters of gold, some whereof weigh 1300. poundes: and he keepes a magnificent and well furnished court. When he trauelleth any whither he rideth vpon a camell, which is lead by some of his noblemen; and so he doth likewise when hee goeth to warfar, and all his souldiers ride vpon horses.
Here are great store of doctors, iudges, priests, and other learned men, that are bountifully maintained at the kings cost and charges. And hither are brought diuers manuscripts or written bookes out of Barbarie, which are sold for more money than any other merchandize.
The inhabitants are people of a gentle and chereful disposition, and spend a great part of the night in singing and dancing through all the streets of the citie: they keep great store of men and women-slaues, and their towne is much in danger of fire: at my second being there halfe the town almost was burnt in fiue howers space.
